## Independent audit (GPT 6.1 Sol) at 45787152069490b719f0750ea8cb98f08674259e

**VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES at `45787152069490b719f0750ea8cb98f08674259e`.**

**Scope:** Fresh cumulative review of the #304 stack dependency plus the new native `expo-updates` package/lock entries, iOS build 6 / Android versionCode 5, runtime policy and extra fingerprint source, channel/environment isolation, launch/offline/error-recovery settings, config validator, publish guard and runbook. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)

**Findings**

- **B1 — inherited #304 blockers, `src/lib/packagePromptGate.ts:16-23` and `src/services/pushTapRouter.ts:65-86`:** this exact tree includes the same fail-open automatic package prompts, missing coach/community nested push routing, and premature lean/coach-wizard tap consumption. Their fixes and behavioral test requirements are recorded once in the independent #304 comment; a stack cannot be approved while those material acceptance findings remain. Update/reconcile the base after the fixes and bind the final stack to a new exact-head audit. [Independent #304 findings](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/304#issuecomment-5922667002)
- **C1 — `package-lock.json` Supabase entry:** this head still resolves `@supabase/supabase-js` 2.106.1, whose actual ESM entry independently fails Hermes compilation at the OTEL dynamic import. Reconcile the approved #307 fix into the native-release tree; do not interpret this PR's green JS unit checks as a successful store build. [Independent #307 evidence](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/307#issuecomment-5922173930)
- **C2 — `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md:133-138`:** embedded/offline launch, update receipt, early-failure recovery and operator rollback remain unexecuted device checks. Keep them as hard gates before the first production publish and retain the installed binary/runtime/update-group identities with the results. Config/Jest cannot prove device recovery. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)
- **C3 — `app.json:13-20` / `scripts/eas-update-guard.js:117-156`:** update signing is absent and the local publish wrapper is governance, not an authorization boundary. The runbook correctly admits that an authorized EAS publisher can bypass the gate from a different file. Restrict actual EAS publish rights to the owner, verify both remote environments and their API/provider variables, and do not claim that a fingerprinted gate file prevents arbitrary publisher-controlled JS. This is the documented residual posture, not a new demonstrated vulnerability. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)
- **C4 — `scripts/validate-app-config.js:745-749`:** `updates.enabled:false` is only a warning and `checkAutomatically` accepts modes other than the documented `ON_LOAD`; future changes could stop the promised OTA behavior while the default validator stays green. Consider testing/enforcing the accepted production behavior separately from “valid configuration.” Current `app.json` has `enabled:true`, `ON_LOAD` and timeout 0. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)

**Positive configuration conclusions**

- The selected fingerprint policy avoids a shared fixed `1.0.0` runtime after native changes; the gate source is an explicit extra fingerprint input and its pinned SHA-256 matches. Preview/production channel and EAS environment names align, the URL matches the project ID, launch timeout is zero, and the candidate does not disable anti-bricking or embedded-update fallback. These are source/config conclusions, not an EAS/device acceptance claim. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)
- The wrapper fails closed for missing/non-true/masked/duplicate remote flag values, rejects mismatched channel/environment and policy hashes, and strips the local flag from lookup/publish children; the remote lookup command's flags are supported by the published CLI reference. No live lookup/publish was performed. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305), [EAS CLI reference](https://docs.expo.dev/eas/cli/)

**Checks run**

- Local `node scripts/validate-app-config.js`: passed, two existing warnings. Local `npx tsc --noEmit`: passed, exit 0. Local `checkPolicyHash()`: no errors, gate SHA-256 `dc62f3799fa2a9503bcd095e2cc16a2a0a8c7b821912a1503c2d81abaff85d48`. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)
- Local `npx jest --maxWorkers=1 scripts/__tests__/easUpdateGuard.test.js scripts/__tests__/validateAppConfig.test.js scripts/__tests__/validateAppConfigUpdates.test.js`: **3 suites / 65 passed**; separate `scripts/__tests__/purchaseGateFingerprint.test.js`: **1 suite / 2 passed**, iOS and Android mutations change the fingerprint with the other fingerprint sources unchanged. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)
- **Local dependency limitation:** these checks used the operator's main-linked install; #305's added `expo-updates` native dependency graph was not present in that shared install. The local mutation proof is not an attestation of the release binary's final fingerprint; I did not run `expo-updates runtimeversion:resolve`, native prebuild/build, remote publish or device tests on this linked graph. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)
- Independently read exact-head CI, including the real fingerprint mutation suite: clean `npm ci`, vendor/config/lint, `npx tsc --noEmit` and full Jest passed **355 suites / 4,803 tests**. The inherited iOS matrix was also independently run on #304 (**13 targeted suites / 242 tests overall**); that reuse is bounded to unchanged inherited source/dependency inputs, not to the new native dependency. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/actions/runs/36777678842/job/110099602779), [Independent #304 checks](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/304#issuecomment-5922667002)

**Merge condition:** close inherited B findings on #304 with both final-head T4 audits, reconcile and freshly attest the resulting stack, retain green exact-head CI and the reviewed OTA/purchase-policy invariants. Before distributing the combined native build, include #307 and prove its build; before production OTA, verify owner publish restrictions, remote environment provisioning, and all four device acceptance checks. No EAS update was published and no code was pushed by this auditor. [PR #305](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305)

AUDIT Claude Opus 5.5 — growth-project-mobile#305 @ 92c25ec81db4cd1e5fd5cf0af766d1d97ab1de03 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

T4 release infra, with a DEP CHANGE (expo-updates). This is my first audit of this PR; Sol's last verdict was at `45787152` ([5922691955](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/305#issuecomment-5922691955)). **A0 / B2 / C1.**

### Verified
- **Dependency.**
  - `expo-updates ~56.0.28` satisfies Expo 56.0.12's bundled `~56.0.19`.
  - The lock delta is 7 additions only, with no removals: expo-updates, expo-eas-client, expo-json-utils, expo-manifests, expo-structured-headers, expo-updates-interface and a nested `arg`. All come from registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity.
  - No JS imports expo-updates.
- **Launch never waits on the network.**
  - `updates.enabled: true`, `checkAutomatically: "ON_LOAD"`, `fallbackToCacheTimeout: 0`.
  - `runtimeVersion: { policy: "fingerprint" }`.
  - The URL matches the project id.
- **Validator.** `validate-app-config.js:769-783` now fails (not warns) on `enabled ≠ true`, `checkAutomatically ≠ ON_LOAD` or `fallbackToCacheTimeout ≠ 0`. This closes Sol C4.
- **Channels.**
  - preview → `preview`, production → `production`, clinic (`extends: production`) → `clinic`. clinic and production use the `production` environment.
  - The validator requires one profile per channel.
- **Purchase gate.** `fingerprint.config.js` makes `src/config/purchaseSurfaces.ts` a fingerprint input. `purchase-policy.sha256` re-pins it, and `fingerprint-gate-check.js` and its test prove that a JS edit to the gate changes the runtime.
- **Prior findings.**
  - Sol B1 is closed: #304 is on main, and this tree is main plus the #305 delta.
  - Sol C1 is closed: #307 is on main, with supabase-js 2.105.0 in the lock.
  - Sol C2 (device checks) and C3 (no update signing; the guard is governance, not authorization) remain release items, and are documented.
- **Merges and checks.**
  - The head merges cleanly with main `2c17c241`, #333 (`eas-profile.js` is identical) and #330.
  - Required checks are SUCCESS: Typecheck/lint/test, Analyze (js-ts) and Analyze (actions). CodeQL is also SUCCESS.

### B-305-5: the runbook's staged rollout bypasses the guard and drops the clinic profile env from the update
- **Evidence:**
  - `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md:162` says "For a risky change use `--rollout-percentage` with the raw command only after the dry run passed".
  - The guard's own header (check 5) and `publishEnv` (`scripts/eas-update-guard.js:228`) exist because `eas update` does not apply eas.json `build.<profile>.env`.
  - A raw `eas update --channel clinic` therefore builds the bundle without clinic's `EXPO_PUBLIC_FF_*` values: CONSULTATION_ONBOARDING, CLIENT_TUTORIAL, COMMUNITY_DM=false and the others.
  - The guard has no rollout option (`:297` passes only channel, environment and message).
- **Impact:** for the clinic rollout cohort, the riskiest update is the one shipped through the unguarded path. It silently flips clinic features in the delivered JS.
- **Minimal fix:**
  1. Add `--rollout-percentage <1-100>` to the guard: validate it as an integer from 1 to 100, and pass it through to `eas-cli update` with `publishEnv`.
  2. Change line 162 to use the guard only.
  3. Add a test that the child gets the flag and the profile env.

### B-305-6: errors from OTA-delivered JS reach Sentry unsymbolicated, and step 5 cannot be done as written
- **Evidence:**
  - Source maps are uploaded only at EAS build time (`@sentry/react-native/expo` plugin, `metro.config.js` Debug IDs; README "Sentry release tracking").
  - An `eas update` bundle has new Debug IDs and no uploaded maps. The guard publishes and exits (`:297-300`).
  - The release stays `<version>+<build>` (`src/services/sentry.ts` `buildReleaseId`), so `docs/OTA_UPDATES.md:163` "Watch Sentry for the new release" has no new release to watch.
- **Impact:** after the first hotfix, every unknown error from the updated JS arrives with minified frames. The owner rule needs unknown errors in Sentry to be actionable, and OTA is the day-1 hotfix path.
- **Minimal fix:**
  1. After a successful publish, have the guard run `npx sentry-expo-upload-sourcemaps dist`, with `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` from the EAS env. If the token is missing, give a named next step; if the upload fails, exit non-zero.
  2. Change step 5 to filter Sentry by the update id (the SDK's expo-updates context) or the channel.
  3. Add a test that the upload runs only after a status-0 publish.

### C-305-7 (operator check): iOS build number for the new binary
- expo-updates is a native change, so a new iOS binary is needed. `ios.buildNumber` is still `"6"`, while android `versionCode` was bumped to 5.
- `appVersionSource` is `local`. If build 6 was already uploaded to App Store Connect, bump to 7 before building. That is still ≥ `IOS_P2P_ONLY_MIN_NATIVE_BUILD = 6`, so the gate is unaffected.

### Release
- This needs a new binary: expo-updates, plus #330's native init, changes the fingerprint. Binaries already built cannot receive OTA.
- Sol C2's four device checks stay hard gates before the first production or clinic publish.
- Restrict EAS publish rights to the owner (Sol C3).

No push, merge, dispatch, build, publish or production action by this auditor.
